subject: SOC 2 renewal: evidence phasing, log export onramp, and amendment proposal
messages:
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <contracts@acme.com>, Tom Willis <tom.willis@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal questions: retention window & evidence export needs

Hi Ben,

As we prepare for our Q4 renewal I wanted to surface a couple of requests from our internal security and audit teams so we can confirm timelines and cost. High level: Acme is looking to extend our retention window for audit logs from 365 days to 540 days for the coming 12-month term, and we need a re-attestation pack for SOC 2 (Type II) that includes the bulk of system logs and a complete evidence inventory.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood provide an evidence matrix that maps controls to artifacts and delivery dates?
- We will need a one-time bulk export of audit logs (approx estimate: 12-18 TB) ahead of our internal audit (target: the week of Dec 6). Can you run a burst export or provide a scalable transfer window?
- Are there constraints around PII in logs that would require redaction or longer lead time?
- Rough cost estimate for extended retention (per GB-month) and one-time burst export.

We'd like to lock timing by Nov 20 if possible to meet audit deadlines. Please loop in whoever owns SOC 2 artifacts and infra exports.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Security, Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_audit_scope_v2.pdf (referenced)

Couple notes from the compliance side: 
- Evidence we can produce quickly (Phase 1, target 7-10 business days): control narratives, configuration snapshots (IAM, network ACLs), change log exports, access review artifacts, and summary audit logs (non-PII).
- Phase 2 (bulk): raw audit log exports, detailed KV/trace logs, and longer history exports will require staging and an agreed delivery mechanism — estimate 14-30 days depending on throughput and whether logs need redaction.
- PII: we mask certain user identifiers in high-volume traces; if Acme requires raw PII-bearing records we need a formal data request and a scoped process (legal signoff).
- For the re-attestation pack we should include: evidence matrix, control owner attestations (signed forms), test results, and the log export manifest. I attached a proposed amendment draft to capture scope/retention.

I will add specific artifact delivery dates once Jonas provides the export timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Compliance & Assurance, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: export options and throughput estimates

Ben / team — technical options for 12-18 TB export (assume compressed logs):
1) Presigned S3 + parallel workers: easiest operationally. We can stage exports into a customer-owned S3 bucket using presigned multipart upload. Estimated wall time: 3-7 days depending on client's ingest concurrency (we can push parallelism on our side).
2) Dedicated burst pool: spin up temporary high-throughput workers and a direct transfer path from our hot archive to an S3 target (or to a secured transfer appliance). Estimated wall time: 24-72 hours for 15 TB if we reserve burst pool and network bandwidth. We need 72 hours notice to schedule and a short IP allowlist window.
3) Physical transfer (appliance): ship encrypted storage device. Longer lead time (logistics) but useful for constrained networks; estimate 7-14 days end-to-end.

Redaction: if Acme requires unmasked PII we must run a scoped export with legal signoff and implement temporary access controls. Redaction increases processing time by ~30-50% depending on the number of fields to mask.

Operational asks for scheduling burst pool: target window, destination S3 details, preferred transfer protocol, and whether Acme wants us to deliver a digest manifest for each object. I'll prepare a runbook and a throughput estimate spreadsheet.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: burst-capacity-estimate.xlsx (estimate)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Pricing and amendment next steps

Hi Sara / Tom — following internal review we have numbers and a proposed amendment draft attached. High level: 
- Retention: increase from 365 to 540 days = incremental $0.012 per GB-month (discounted for existing committed volume). We applied Acme's current average monthly volume to estimate total delta; details in the attached spreadsheet.
- One-time burst export options: (a) Presigned S3 transfer: one-time ops fee $3,500 + standard egress; (b) Dedicated burst pool: one-time reservation fee $12,000 (includes 72-hour reserved window) + egress; (c) Physical appliance: $6,000 + shipping and handling.
- Credits: we can apply a one-time credit toward the reservation fee if Acme signs the amendment and extends term to 15 months.

Next steps we propose:
1) Review the attached proposed-amendment-draft.pdf and the two spreadsheets for price detail.
2) Schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday 11/10 to walk pricing and runbook and confirm export path. 11:00-11:30am PT or 2:00-2:30pm PT available.
3) Target amendment signature by Nov 20 to meet your audit timeline; if you need legal redlines we can accept them as comments in the PDF and turn around within 48 hours.

Please let us know which export option you prefer and which call time works.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Laura Bennett
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
